headline: ReSteer identifies and fixes poor task steerability in multitask robot policies for interactive deployment
summary: Despite strong multi-task pretraining, existing policies exhibit poor task steerability: a robot may ignore a new instruction when already committed to a different task. ReSteer introduces a framework to quantify steerability via trajectory distribution overlap, a steerability estimator for identifying problematic states, a steerable data generator, and a self-refinement pipeline. It improves steerability by 11% in simulation and demonstrates critical impact for interactive real-world deployment.
abstract: Despite strong multi-task pretraining, existing policies often exhibit poor task steerability. For example, a robot may fail to respond to a new instruction 'put the bowl in the sink' when moving towards the oven, executing 'close the oven', even though it can complete both tasks when executed separately. We propose ReSteer, a framework to quantify and improve task steerability in multitask robot policies. We conduct an exhaustive evaluation of state-of-the-art policies, revealing a common lack of steerability. We find that steerability is associated with limited overlap among training task trajectory distributions, and introduce a proxy metric to measure this overlap from policy behavior. Building on this insight, ReSteer improves steerability via three components: (i) a steerability estimator that identifies low-steerability states without full-rollout evaluation, (ii) a steerable data generator that synthesizes motion segments from these states, and (iii) a self-refinement pipeline that improves policy steerability using the generated data. In simulation on LIBERO, ReSteer improves steerability by 11% over 18k rollouts. In real-world experiments, we show that improved steerability is critical for interactive use, enabling users to instruct robots to perform any task at any time. We hope this work motivates further study on quantifying steerability and data collection strategies for large robot policies.
notes: Moderate — quantifies and improves task steerability in multitask robot policies, relevant to interactive deployment of VLAs

title: Emergent Neural Automaton Policies: Learning Symbolic Structure from Visuomotor Trajectories
authors: Yiyuan Pan, Xusheng Luo, Hanjiang Hu, Peiqi Yu, Changliu Liu
headline: Neuro-symbolic policies with emergent Mealy machines outperform VLAs by 27% in low-data regimes
summary: ENAP infers a Mealy state machine from visuomotor demonstrations using adaptive clustering and the L* algorithm, creating an interpretable high-level planner that guides a low-level residual network for continuous control via behavior cloning. The explicit discrete-continuous structure achieves high sample efficiency without task-specific labels. On complex manipulation and long-horizon tasks, ENAP outperforms state-of-the-art end-to-end VLA policies by up to 27% in low-data regimes.
abstract: Scaling robot learning to long-horizon tasks remains a formidable challenge. While end-to-end policies often lack the structural priors needed for effective long-term reasoning, traditional neuro-symbolic methods rely heavily on hand-crafted symbolic priors. To address the issue, we introduce ENAP (Emergent Neural Automaton Policy), a framework that allows a bi-level neuro-symbolic policy adaptively emerge from visuomotor demonstrations. Specifically, we first employ adaptive clustering and an extension of the L* algorithm to infer a Mealy state machine from visuomotor data, which serves as an interpretable high-level planner capturing latent task modes. Then, this discrete structure guides a low-level reactive residual network to learn precise continuous control via behavior cloning (BC). By explicitly modeling the task structure with discrete transitions and continuous residuals, ENAP achieves high sample efficiency and interpretability without requiring task-specific labels. Extensive experiments on complex manipulation and long-horizon tasks demonstrate that ENAP outperforms state-of-the-art (SoTA) end-to-end VLA policies by up to 27% in low-data regimes, while offering a structured representation of robotic intent.
notes: Moderate — RSS 2026; neuro-symbolic framework learning interpretable Mealy machines from visuomotor data, connects to verification through interpretability

title: mimic-video: Video-Action Models for Generalizable Robot Control Beyond VLAs
authors: Jonas Pai, Liam Achenbach, Victoriano Montesinos, Benedek Forrai, Oier Mees, Elvis Nava
headline: Video-action model with flow-matching decoder achieves 10x sample efficiency over traditional VLAs
summary: mimic-video pairs a pretrained Internet-scale video model with a flow matching-based action decoder conditioned on the video model's latent representations. The video backbone captures both semantic and physical dynamics priors, while the decoder serves as an inverse dynamics model generating low-level actions from latent video-space plans. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on simulated and real-world manipulation with 10x sample efficiency and 2x convergence speed improvement over VLA architectures.
abstract: Prevailing Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) for robotic manipulation are built upon vision-language backbones pretrained on large-scale, but disconnected static web data. As a result, despite improved semantic generalization, the policy must implicitly infer complex physical dynamics and temporal dependencies solely from robot trajectories. This reliance creates an unsustainable data burden, necessitating continuous, large-scale expert data collection to compensate for the lack of innate physical understanding. We contend that while vision-language pretraining effectively captures semantic priors, it remains blind to physical causality. A more effective paradigm leverages video to jointly capture semantics and visual dynamics during pretraining, thereby isolating the remaining task of low-level control. To this end, we introduce mimic-video, a novel Video-Action Model (VAM) that pairs a pretrained Internet-scale video model with a flow matching-based action decoder conditioned on its latent representations. The decoder serves as an Inverse Dynamics Model (IDM), generating low-level robot actions from the latent representation of video-space action plans. Our extensive evaluation shows that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks, improving sample efficiency by 10x and convergence speed by 2x compared to traditional VLA architectures.
notes: High — RSS 2026; video-action model pairing pretrained video model with flow-matching action decoder, 10x sample efficiency over VLAs

title: One Demonstration Is Enough for Real-World Robotic Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yuwan Liu, Hongze Yu, Song Liu, Yuhan Wang, Junge Zhang, Yaodong Yang, Yuanpei Chen, Ceyao Zhang
matched_interests: Reinforcement learning|Safe & robust robot control|Active learning
headline: AutoSERL achieves 100% success on insertion tasks using just one demonstration with automated safe exploration
summary: AutoSERL leverages a single demonstration to fully automate real-world robot RL intervention, using three mechanisms: sliding window intervention for guided exploration, a safety recovery mechanism for failure state correction, and an automatic intervention termination criterion. Evaluated on six contact-intensive manipulation tasks across two platforms, it outperforms SERL with 20 demonstrations, behavior cloning, and one-shot imitation baselines, achieving 100% success on insertion tasks.
abstract: Learning effective robot control policies on physical hardware is challenging due to costly data collection and the difficulty of reward specification. Prior work has incorporated demonstrations into reinforcement learning (RL), yet existing approaches either require large numbers of demonstrations or depend on continuous human intervention during training. To address these limitations, we present AutoSERL, a framework that leverages a single demonstration to fully automate the intervention process in real-world robot RL. The framework includes three complementary mechanisms to accomplish certain tasks: a sliding window intervention mechanism that continuously guides exploration to prevent local optima and unsafe deviations, a safety recovery mechanism that detects and corrects failure states via predefined trajectory recovery points, and an intervention termination criterion that automatically disables guidance once the policy can independently complete the task, preserving its exploration advantage. We evaluate AutoSERL on six contact-intensive manipulation tasks across two robot platforms, spanning insertion, hanging, and hinge-based tasks. AutoSERL consistently outperforms SERL initialized with 20 demonstrations, behavior cloning, and MILES -- a dedicated one-shot imitation learning baseline -- across all tasks while matching HIL-SERL, achieves 100% success rate on insertion tasks, and demonstrates improved robustness to positional variations, all from a single demonstration.
notes: Moderate — one-shot real-world RL with automated intervention and safety recovery from a single demonstration

title: SafeDojo: Safe Reinforcement Learning for VLA via Interactive World Model
authors: Kai Tang, Peidong Jia, Zhong Chu, Jixian Wu, Rui Ma, Jiajun Cao, Fangyuan Zhao, Sixiang Chen, Yichen Guo, Xiaowei Chi, Chun-Kai Fan, Kevin Zhang, Jinchang Xu, Fubing Yang, Weishi Mi, Xiaozhu Ju, Jian Tang, Shanghang Zhang
matched_interests: Safe & robust robot control|Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs)|World models for robotics|Reinforcement learning
headline: First model-based safe RL framework for VLAs learns safe actions through world model imagination
summary: SafeDojo is the first model-based safe RL framework for vision-language-action policies. It performs online RL on top of an interactive video world model that generates action-conditioned future predictions, using a ResNet success classifier and a lightweight safety head to jointly assess task execution and trajectory safety. A Lagrangian-based constrained GRPO objective balances task reward and safety cost. It achieves best aggregate performance on SafeLIBERO and demonstrates strong safe-success rates on real-world Franka deployment.
abstract: Safe control is a prerequisite for real-world embodied intelligence, for which safe reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising paradigm. However, existing safe reinforcement learning methods either require costly real-world exploration or depend on hand-crafted safety functions. Neither scales to vision-language-action models deployed in open-world physical environments. We propose SafeDojo, the first model-based safe reinforcement learning framework for vision-language-action policies designed to learn safe actions through world model-based imagination. Specifically, SafeDojo performs online reinforcement learning on top of an interactive video world model. The world model generates action-conditioned future predictions, from which a tailored ResNet success classifier estimates per-step task progress from imagined frames and a lightweight safety head predicts per-step safety costs from latent context together with the proposed action chunk, enabling simultaneous assessment of task execution and trajectory safety. The decoupled task-reward and safety-cost signals are balanced through a Lagrangian-based constrained GRPO objective, enabling coordinated improvement of task success and safety under explicit constraints. On SafeLIBERO, SafeDojo achieves the best aggregate task success, safe success, and execution efficiency among inference-time safety, model-free RL, and model-based RL baselines, with the best average safe-success rate on both levels and an 8.25 percentage-point improvement over the strongest baseline on Level I. Real-world Franka deployment further shows the best average task and safe-success rates across five tasks. Our results position world model-based safe reinforcement learning as a scalable and generalizable path toward safe embodied intelligence.
notes: High — first model-based safe RL framework for VLAs using world model imagination with Lagrangian safety constraints

title: ELASTIC: Efficiently Learning to Adaptively Scale Test-Time Compute for Generative Control Policies
authors: Andrew Zou Li, Gokul Swamy, Yonatan Bisk, Andrea Bajcsy
headline: Learns state-dependent test-time compute schedules that Pareto-dominate fixed scaling for diffusion control policies
summary: ELASTIC learns state-dependent test-time compute schedules for generative control policies, allocating compute across two axes: sequential scaling (more denoising steps to refine actions) and parallel scaling (sampling candidate actions to search across policy modes). Since the optimal allocation is state-, task-, and policy-dependent, ELASTIC learns when to explore broadly versus refine precisely. Across simulated manipulation benchmarks with diffusion policies, it Pareto-dominates fixed and single-axis scaling baselines at matched compute budgets.
abstract: ELASTIC is an algorithm that learns state-dependent test-time compute schedules for generative control policies (GCPs). Test-time compute can be allocated along two axes: sequential scaling, which increases denoising steps to refine actions, and parallel scaling, which samples multiple candidate actions to search across modes of the policy distribution. The optimal allocation of sequential and parallel compute is hard to know a priori as it is state-, task-, and policy-dependent. For example, early stages of a grasp may benefit from broader parallel exploration, while near-contact phases may require more sequential refinement for precision. Across simulated manipulation benchmarks with diffusion policies, ELASTIC Pareto-dominates fixed and single-axis scaling baselines at matched compute budgets.
notes: Alert: Bajcsy (new articles). High - adaptive test-time compute (sequential/parallel scaling) for generative/diffusion control policies

title: Foresight: Failure Detection for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation with Action-Conditioned World Model Latents
authors: Haoran Zhang, Yifu Lu, Boyang Wang, Xuhui Kang, Yen-Ling Kuo, Zezhou Cheng, Mengdi Wang, Odest Chadwicke Jenkins
matched_interests: World models for robotics|Latent-space safety analysis|Conformal prediction|Verification of visuomotor policies|Uncertainty quantification & failure detection for learned policies
headline: Detects manipulation failures from action-conditioned world-model latents, calibrated with functional conformal prediction
summary: Foresight is a failure-detection framework that monitors long-horizon manipulation by reading latent representations from an action-conditioned world model, trained using only final task-level success/failure labels. It uses functional conformal prediction (FCP) to adaptively calibrate detection thresholds. It is evaluated with state-of-the-art VLA policies on LIBERO-Long, ManiSkill-Long, and BEHAVIOR-1K, and validated on real ReactorX-200 and Franka arms. The work sits at the intersection of world models, latent-space safety, and conformal monitoring of learned policies.
abstract: Foresight is a failure detection framework that monitors manipulation trajectories using latent representations from an action-conditioned world model, trained using only final task-level success or failure labels. The method uses functional conformal prediction (FCP) to calibrate detection thresholds adaptively. The approach is evaluated with state-of-the-art vision-language-action policies in simulation on LIBERO-Long, ManiSkill-Long, and BEHAVIOR-1K, compared against state-of-the-art failure detection methods, and validated on real robots with three long-horizon tasks on a ReactorX-200 arm and one task on a Franka arm. Authors are from the University of Michigan, Princeton University, and the University of Virginia.
notes: Alert: Majumdar/Bajcsy (related). Core - failure detection for VLA policies via conformal prediction on action-conditioned world-model latents

title: Scenario Generation for Testing of Autonomous Driving Systems Using Real-World Failure Records
authors: Aditya Parashar, Chuchu Fan
matched_interests: Data-driven verification|Safe & robust robot control|Adversarial robustness of robot policies
headline: Generates autonomous-driving test scenarios from real-world crash records using LLM-parsed narratives
summary: This work proposes a scenario-generation pipeline that mines categorical and contextual information from historical failure/crash records of autonomous driving systems. It builds a test suite of scenario templates parameterized by categorical crash features (e.g., pre-crash vehicle movements, road type), and uses large language models to transform natural-language crash narratives into system-specific scenarios. The generated scenarios serve as initialization for low-level testing methods such as Bayesian optimization, MCMC sampling, and gradient-based optimization.
abstract: To ensure safe on-road behavior, pre-deployment testing of autonomous driving systems is essential. This work proposes a scenario generation pipeline that uses categorical and contextual information from historical failure records of autonomous driving systems, leveraging natural-language narratives from crash records. The approach constructs a test suite of scenario templates parameterized using categorical features available in crash records, such as pre-crash vehicle movements and road type. Crash records provide natural-language descriptions of incidents, called narratives, which offer detailed insights about failure conditions. The work adopts large language models (LLMs) to transform crash narratives into system-specific scenarios. The proposed approach can be used for initial scenario generation, over which low-level testing methods such as Bayesian Optimization, MCMC sampling, and gradient-based optimization can be deployed.
notes: Alert: Fan (new articles). Core - data-driven scenario/test generation for verifying autonomous driving systems from real-world failure records

title: VLAFlow: A Unified Training Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models via Co-training and Future Latent Alignment
authors: G Xia, F Li, H Ji, L Ren, F Feng, K Zhan, Y Xie
headline: Controlled comparison of four VLA training objectives under one flow-matching architecture on a 5,000-hour robot corpus
summary: VLAFlow is a unified flow-matching framework for controlled comparison of VLA training objectives, evaluating four paradigms under the same pi0-style architecture, shared VLM backbone, action expert, and 14-dimensional action space: action-only modeling, language-supervised co-training, future latent alignment, and their combination. Training uses OXEMix, a heterogeneous ~5,000-hour robot corpus from DROID, OpenX-Embodiment, OpenX-Augmented, and RoboCOIN. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and SimplerEnv show action-only pre-training is sensitive to heterogeneous data, motivating auxiliary objectives.
abstract: VLAFlow (Vision-Language-Action Flow) is a unified flow-matching framework for controlled comparison of VLA training objectives. The framework evaluates four training paradigms under the same pi0-style architecture, shared VLM backbone, action expert, and 14-dimensional action space: action-only modeling (MindPI), language-supervised co-training (MindLPI), future latent alignment (MindWPI), and their combination (MindLWPI). The research uses a heterogeneous robot corpus called OXEMix, containing approximately 5,000 hours of data from DROID, OpenX-Embodiment, OpenX-Augmented, and RoboCOIN. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and SimplerEnv show that action-only pre-training is sensitive to heterogeneous data.
notes: Alert: Majumdar (citation). High - controlled comparison of VLA training objectives under a unified flow-matching framework [residual -1: VLA training study; flow matching is architectural, not a novel control/verification method]

title: PAIWorld: A 3D-Consistent World Foundation Model for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Yuhang Huang, Jiazhao Zhang, Xuan Lv, Junyan Xu, Zhiyuan Yu, Ruizhen Hu, Kai Xu
headline: Multi-view world foundation model with geometry-aware attention for 3D-consistent manipulation simulation
summary: PAIWorld is a world foundation model (simulator) that adds explicit multi-view 3D consistency for robotic manipulation, addressing single-view WFMs that cause cross-view object drift, depth inconsistency, and texture misalignment. It introduces Geometry-Aware Cross-View Attention blocks that establish an explicit pathway across egocentric, eye-to-hand, and wrist-mounted views, and a Geometric Rotary Position Embedding that encodes camera-ray directions. The result is a geometrically consistent generative simulator suited to multi-camera robot policy learning.
abstract: World foundation models (WFMs) are powerful simulators, yet they predominantly operate in a single-view setting and lack the multi-view 3D consistency required for robotic manipulation. While robotic systems rely on multiple cameras (egocentric, eye-to-hand, and wrist-mounted) for policy learning, current multi-view world models simply concatenate view tokens without explicit geometric reasoning, causing cross-view object drift, depth inconsistency, and texture misalignment. PAIWorld addresses this through three core components: (1) Geometry-Aware Cross-View Attention blocks that establish an explicit pathway across views, (2) Geometric Rotary Position Embedding that encodes camera ray directions, and additional geometric-reasoning mechanisms for 3D-consistent generation.
notes: Alert: Majumdar (related). High - multi-view 3D-consistent world foundation model (simulator) for robotic manipulation

title: DVG-WM: Disentangled Video Generation Enables Efficient Embodied World Model for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Z Shan, Z Wu, X Wang, Z Zhu, Z Wang
matched_interests: World models for robotics|Flow matching|Diffusion models
headline: Disentangles dynamics from visual synthesis, using flow matching for a 3.97x faster embodied world model
summary: DVG-WM is a video-based embodied world model that decomposes world modeling into dynamics learning and visual synthesis to resolve the entanglement between low-level temporal reasoning and high-resolution frame generation. Conditioned on an initial observation and language instruction, it first previews a plausible sequence of intermediate visual states and then refines them into high-fidelity video. A cascading mechanism uses flow matching to map dynamics directly to video latents, with a latent degradation mechanism to regenerate contact-rich detail. Experiments on LIBERO and real-world platforms show improved video quality with up to 3.97x acceleration.
abstract: Video-based embodied world models provide an appealing substrate for robotic manipulation by predicting future states, yet current approaches remain limited by a fundamental entanglement: accurately modeling dynamics typically requires low-level temporal reasoning, while producing high-resolution frames demands expansive visual synthesis according to high-level semantics. To solve this dilemma, the authors present Disentangled Video Generation World Model (DVG-WM), an efficient framework that explicitly decomposes world modeling into dynamics learning and visual synthesis. Conditioned on an initial observation and a language instruction, the model first generates a plausible sequence of intermediate visual states to preview the physical interaction and refines them to obtain high-fidelity videos. An efficient cascading mechanism is proposed, where DVG-WM leverages flow matching to directly map the dynamics to video latents, and introduces a latent degradation mechanism to enable the capability of regenerating contact-rich details. Experiments on LIBERO and real-world platforms demonstrate improved video quality with up to 3.97x acceleration.
notes: Alert: Majumdar (related). High - disentangles dynamics vs. visual synthesis; flow matching maps dynamics to video latents for efficient embodied world model

title: Uncertainty Quantification via Invariant-Measure Conformal Prediction
authors: M Bakhtiaridoust, D Baumann, S Deka
matched_interests: Conformal prediction|Data-driven verification|Uncertainty quantification & failure detection for learned policies
headline: Invariant-measure conformal prediction restores coverage guarantees for temporally-dependent learned dynamical systems
summary: This paper introduces invariant-measure conformal prediction (imCP) for uncertainty quantification of learned stochastic dynamical systems, a setting where standard conformal prediction fails because trajectory data violate exchangeability: data are temporally dependent, state distributions evolve, and recursive prediction errors accumulate. By reasoning about the system's invariant measure, imCP aims to provide valid distribution-free coverage guarantees in safety-critical control and monitoring. The method targets the exact regime relevant to data-driven verification of learned dynamics.
abstract: Uncertainty quantification for learned stochastic dynamical systems is essential in safety-critical tasks such as control and monitoring. Standard conformal prediction provides finite-sample coverage guarantees under exchangeability, but this assumption is typically violated in dynamical systems because trajectory data are temporally dependent, state distributions evolve, and recursive prediction errors accumulate. This paper proposes an invariant-measure conformal prediction (imCP) approach that restores distribution-free coverage guarantees for learned stochastic dynamical systems by leveraging the system's invariant measure. [Abstract truncated from Google Scholar alert snippet.]

title: Data-Driven Control Based on Control Barrier Functions with Recursive Feasibility Guarantee
authors: J Liao, W Xiang
matched_interests: Data-driven verification|Control Barrier Functions (CBFs)|Safe & robust robot control
headline: Identification-free data-driven CBF control with recursive feasibility and robustness from sampled data
summary: This paper proposes an identification-free, data-driven control framework built on control barrier functions that enforces hard state and input constraints at each step while ensuring recursive feasibility and robustness. From sampled data, the authors derive a tractable uncertainty description used directly for safe control synthesis, bypassing explicit system identification. The approach targets safety guarantees for systems known only through data, aligning with data-driven verification of black-box dynamics.
abstract: We propose an identification-free, data-driven control framework that enforces hard state and input constraints at each step, ensuring recursive feasibility and robustness. From sampled data, we derive a tractable uncertainty description for the system and integrate it with control barrier function conditions to synthesize safe control inputs with guarantees, without requiring an explicit system model. title: Safe Flow Q-Learning: Offline Safe Reinforcement Learning with Reachability-Based Flow Policies and Conformal Prediction
authors: M Tayal, M Tayal, R Prakash
venue: Workshop on Agents in the Wild (OpenReview)
matched_interests: Reinforcement learning|Flow matching|Conformal prediction|Hamilton-Jacobi reachability|Safe & robust robot control
headline: Combines HJ-reachability safety values, a one-step flow policy, and conformal prediction for offline safe RL
summary: Safe Flow Q-Learning (SafeFQL) extends Flow Q-Learning to offline safe reinforcement learning, targeting reward-maximizing policies from static datasets under strict safety constraints. Rather than soft expected-cost objectives or iterative generative inference, it combines a Hamilton-Jacobi reachability-inspired safety value function with an efficient one-step flow policy and calibrates constraints with conformal prediction. The design targets safety-critical real-time control and unites several core threads: flow policies, reachability, and conformal guarantees.
abstract: Offline safe reinforcement learning (RL) seeks reward-maximizing policies from static datasets under strict safety constraints. Existing methods often rely on soft expected-cost objectives or iterative generative inference, which can be insufficient for safety-critical real-time control. We propose Safe Flow Q-Learning (SafeFQL), which extends FQL to safe offline RL by combining a Hamilton-Jacobi reachability-inspired safety value function with an efficient one-step flow policy. SafeFQL learns the safety value function and uses conformal prediction to calibrate constraint satisfaction. [Abstract truncated from Google Scholar alert snippet.]

title: Bridging Safety and Performance in Autonomous Systems using Offline Reinforcement Learning
authors: M Tayal, M Tayal, R Prakash
venue: Workshop on Agents in the Wild (OpenReview)
headline: Offline safe RL with hard-constraint formulation robust to distributional shift
summary: This workshop paper tackles safe offline reinforcement learning for deploying autonomous systems in safety-critical settings without online exploration. The authors argue that many existing safe offline RL approaches use soft constraint formulations that can permit safety violations and are sensitive to distributional shift. They instead pursue a formulation providing stronger safety guarantees while maintaining performance from fixed datasets. It is a companion to the same authors' Safe Flow Q-Learning work.
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) offers a promising framework for deploying autonomous systems in safety-critical settings without the risks of online exploration. However, learning policies that simultaneously achieve high performance and strong safety guarantees from fixed datasets remains a fundamental challenge. Many existing safe offline RL approaches typically rely on soft constraint formulations, which may permit safety violations and are sensitive to distributional shift. In contrast, this work develops a formulation that enforces stronger safety guarantees while preserving performance. [Abstract truncated from Google Scholar alert snippet.]

title: Context-Triggered Robust MPC for Temporal Logic Specifications
authors: A. B. Kordabad, S. P. Nayak, S. Soudjani, A. K. Schmuck
headline: Robust MPC synthesis for context-dependent temporal logic via reach-avoid-stay certificates
summary: This paper synthesizes robust feedback controllers for discrete-time linear systems satisfying context-dependent linear temporal logic specifications under additive bounded disturbances. Building on results that reduce context-triggered temporal logic synthesis to context-dependent reach-avoid-stay (cRAS) objectives, it focuses on the low-level control synthesis problem using certificate-based methods within a robust MPC scheme. It is control-theoretic with no learning component, hence tangential to the data-driven focus.
abstract: We consider the problem of synthesizing robust feedback controllers for discrete-time linear systems that ensure the satisfaction of context-dependent linear temporal logic specifications in the presence of additive bounded disturbances. Building on existing results that reduce context-triggered temporal logic synthesis to the realization of context-dependent reach-avoid-stay (cRAS) objectives, we focus on the corresponding low-level control synthesis problem. We first employ certificate-based methods to construct robust controllers within a model predictive control scheme. [Abstract truncated from Google Scholar alert snippet.]

title: Learning from Demonstration via Spatiotemporal Tubes for Unknown Euler-Lagrange Systems
authors: R Das, P Shankar, V Buereddy, R Prakash, P Jagtap
headline: Treats demonstrations as a data-driven safety specification via learned spatiotemporal tubes
summary: STT-LfD is a learning-from-demonstration framework that integrates motion learning with control for unknown Euler-Lagrange systems. Instead of tracking a fixed reference, it treats demonstrations as a data-driven safety specification: using heteroscedastic Gaussian Processes, it learns Spatiotemporal Tubes (STTs) as an intent envelope capturing time-varying precision requirements of a task. A closed-form controller then keeps the system within the tube, yielding a demonstrations-as-constraints style of safety.
abstract: We present STT-LfD, a unified Learning from Demonstration (LfD) framework that integrates motion learning with control for unknown Euler-Lagrange systems. Unlike traditional decoupled approaches that track a fixed reference, the proposed method treats demonstrations as a data-driven safety specification. Using heteroscedastic Gaussian Processes, STT-LfD learns Spatiotemporal Tubes (STTs) as an intent envelope that capture time-varying precision requirements of a task. A closed-form control law then guarantees the system evolves within the learned tube. [Abstract truncated from Google Scholar alert snippet.]

title: The FaBRIC Strategy for Verifying Neural Feedback Systems
authors: Samuel I. Akinwande, Sydney M. Katz, Mykel J. Kochenderfer, Clark Barrett
matched_interests: Data-driven verification|Hamilton-Jacobi reachability|Safe & robust robot control
headline: Forward+backward reachability integration dramatically improves neural feedback system verification
summary: FaBRIC introduces algorithms for computing over- and underapproximations of backward reachable sets for nonlinear neural feedback systems, and integrates them with forward reachability analysis. The combined Forward and Backward Reachability Integration for Certification (FaBRIC) algorithm significantly outperforms prior state of the art on representative benchmarks for verifying reach-avoid specifications in neural-network-controlled dynamical systems.
abstract: Forward reachability analysis is a dominant approach for verifying reach-avoid specifications in neural feedback systems, i.e., dynamical systems controlled by neural networks, and a number of directions have been proposed and studied. In contrast, far less attention has been given to backward reachability analysis for these systems, in part because of the limited scalability of known techniques. In this work, we begin to address this gap by introducing new algorithms for computing both over- and underapproximations of backward reachable sets for nonlinear neural feedback systems. We also describe and implement an integration of these backward reachability techniques with existing ones for forward analysis. We call the resulting algorithm Forward and Backward Reachability Integration for Certification (FaBRIC). We evaluate our algorithms on a representative set of benchmarks and show that they significantly outperform the prior state of the art.
notes: Core — forward+backward reachability verification of neural feedback systems; directly relevant to verification of learned controllers

title: Safety Certificate against Latent Variables with Partially Unidentifiable Dynamics
authors: Haoming Jing, Yorie Nakahira
matched_interests: Data-driven verification|Latent-space safety analysis|Safe & robust robot control
headline: Probabilistic safety certificates for systems with latent variables using causal RL for long-term risk
summary: This paper proposes probabilistic safety certificates for systems with latent variables that make dynamics partially unidentifiable. A key enabler is formulating invariance conditions in probability space, constructable from observed statistics despite distribution shifts. The certificate continuously finds feasible actions controlling long-term risk. This is the first work integrating causal RL with safety certificate design for systems with latent variables.
abstract: Many systems contain latent variables that make their dynamics partially unidentifiable or cause distribution shifts in the observed statistics between offline and online data. However, existing control techniques often assume access to complete dynamics or perfect simulators with fully observable states, which are necessary to verify whether the system remains within a safe set (forward invariance) or safe actions are consistently feasible at all times. To address this limitation, we propose a technique for designing probabilistic safety certificates for systems with latent variables. A key technical enabler is the formulation of invariance conditions in probability space, which can be constructed using observed statistics in the presence of distribution shifts due to latent variables. We use this invariance condition to construct a safety certificate that can be implemented efficiently in real-time control. The proposed safety certificate can continuously find feasible actions that control long-term risk to stay within tolerance. Stochastic safe control and (causal) reinforcement learning have been studied in isolation until now. To the best of our knowledge, the proposed work is the first to use causal reinforcement learning to quantify long-term risk for the design of safety certificates. This integration enables safety certificates to efficiently ensure longterm safety in the presence of latent variables. The effectiveness of the proposed safety certificate is demonstrated in numerical simulations.
notes: Core — safety certificates for partially unidentifiable systems with latent variables; directly relevant to data-driven verification of black-box systems [residual +1: directly addresses verification under latent/unidentifiable dynamics, core to black-box verification]

title: Let the Dynamics Flow: Stable Flow Matching Dynamical Systems
authors: Rodrigo Perez-Dattari, Francisco Leiva, Andrea Testa, Leonel Rozo, Javier Ruiz-del-Solar, Noemie Jaquier
matched_interests: Flow matching|Imitation learning|Safe & robust robot control
headline: Flow matching with formal Lyapunov stability guarantees for safe multimodal robot motion generation
summary: SFMDS bridges high-capacity generative modeling and formal Lyapunov stability guarantees by parametrizing dynamical systems via flow matching while constraining the model to a family of stable solutions. Two variants are proposed: a soft penalty constraint and a hard structural constraint embedded in the architecture. Experiments on benchmarks, simulation, and a humanoid robot demonstrate stable, scalable, multimodal dynamical systems.
abstract: Flow matching has recently emerged as a powerful approach for imitation learning, enabling scalable, expressive, and multimodal motion policies. However, incorporating formal stability guarantees into these generative models, a prerequisite to ensure safe and generalizable robot behaviors, remains a significant challenge. While modeling robot motions as dynamical systems allows for such stability-based inductive biases, existing frameworks struggle to capture the rich action distributions inherent in complex robotic tasks. This paper introduces Stable Flow Matching Dynamical Systems (SFMDS), a novel framework that bridges the gap between high-capacity generative modeling and formal Lyapunov stability guarantees. SFMDS parametrizes dynamical systems via flow matching while simultaneously constraining the model to a family of stable solutions. We propose two variants: a soft constraint based on a penalty term, and a hard structural constraint embedded directly in the model architecture. We further extend both formulations to Lie groups. Experiments on benchmark datasets, in simulation, and on a humanoid robot show that SFMDS learns stable, scalable, and multimodal dynamical systems in low- and high-dimensional state spaces, enabling safe and expressive robot motion generation.
notes: Core — flow matching with formal Lyapunov stability guarantees; intersects safety verification with generative policy learning

title: WarmPrior: Straightening Flow-Matching Policies with Temporal Priors
authors: Sinjae Kang, Chanyoung Kim, Kaixin Wang, Li Zhao, Kimin Lee
headline: Temporal action-history priors straighten flow paths, boosting manipulation success and RL sample efficiency
summary: WarmPrior replaces the standard Gaussian source distribution in flow-matching policies with a temporally grounded prior from recent action history. This produces straighter probability paths (echoing optimal-transport couplings in Rectified Flow), consistently improving success rates on robotic manipulation tasks. Beyond behavior cloning, WarmPrior also reshapes exploration in prior-space RL, improving sample efficiency.
abstract: Generative policies based on diffusion and flow matching have become a dominant paradigm for visuomotor robotic control. We show that replacing the standard Gaussian source distribution with WarmPrior, a simple temporally grounded prior constructed from readily available recent action history, consistently improves success rates on robotic manipulation tasks. We trace this gain to markedly straighter probability paths, echoing the effect of optimal-transport couplings in Rectified Flow. Beyond standard behavior cloning, WarmPrior also reshapes the exploration distribution in prior-space reinforcement learning, improving both sample efficiency and final performance. Collectively, these results identify the source distribution as an important and underexplored design axis in generative robot control. Project page: https://sinnnj.github.io/WarmPrior/.
notes: High — source distribution design axis for flow matching policies; relevant to diffusion/flow policy methodology

title: AEGIS: A Backup Reflex for Physical AI
authors: Josef Chen
matched_interests: Verification of visuomotor policies|Safe & robust robot control
headline: Activation-probe early warning switches to stronger policy mid-trajectory, recovering 10% of lost rollouts
summary: AEGIS uses a lightweight probe on a weak policy's frozen activations to detect high-risk steps before failure compounds. When flagged, control switches to a stronger policy only for those steps. On LIBERO-Spatial, AEGIS recovers 10.1% of lost trajectories versus 4.6% for blind escalation, activating the stronger policy on only 38% of steps.
abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation tends to fail gradually: one bad step degrades the state, and the policy spirals into a basin from which it cannot recover. The failure is often visible before it happens. We introduce AEGIS (Activation-probe Early-warning, Gated Inference Switching), a selective escalation method that uses a lightweight probe on a weak policy's frozen activations to detect high-risk steps while there is still time to act. When the probe flags a step, control switches to a stronger separate policy, but only for the steps that need it. On LIBERO-Spatial, AEGIS recovers 10.1% of the trajectories the weak policy alone loses, versus 4.6% for budget-matched blind escalation and 5.1% for a random-trigger placebo.
notes: High — runtime failure detection and policy switching; related to runtime verification of learned policies

title: ForesightSafety-VLA: A Unified Diagnostic Safety Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Mingyang Lyu, Yinqian Sun, Yiyang Jia, Sicheng Shen, Moquan Sha, Huangrui Li, Feifei Zhao, Yi Zeng
matched_interests: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs)|Adversarial robustness of robot policies|Verification of visuomotor policies
headline: 13-category safety taxonomy benchmark reveals VLA safety is tightly coupled to perception and grounding
summary: ForesightSafety-VLA defines a 13-category safety taxonomy covering physical interaction, instruction-side, and perception-side safety. It evaluates VLA policies under three dimensions of variation (scene structure, language, visual observation) with process-level risk metrics. Even the strongest policy incurs non-trivial safety cost, and perception/structure variation causes stronger degradation than language variation.
abstract: In embodied intelligence, safety is a prerequisite for reliable robot deployment in the physical world. Current vision-language-action (VLA) models continue to advance toward general-purpose task capability, yet their embodied safety limits remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we introduce ForesightSafety-VLA, a diagnostic benchmark that makes safety the primary evaluation target for VLA systems. We define a 13-category safety taxonomy covering physical interaction safety (Safe-Core), instruction-side safety (Safe-Lang), and perception-side safety (Safe-Vis), and evaluate policies under three controlled dimensions of variation -- scene structure, language command, and visual observation -- so that failure sources can be diagnosed rather than hidden in a single aggregate score. Beyond binary task success, ForesightSafety-VLA measures process-level risk through cumulative safety cost (CC) and risk exposure time (RET), together with a four-quadrant decomposition of safe/unsafe success and failure. We instantiate 66 safety-augmented base scenarios in RoboTwin across 5 embodiments and report results on representative VLA baselines. Across the evaluated baselines, even the strongest policy incurs non-trivial safety cost and unsafe nominal success, while structure and visual variation induce substantially stronger safety degradation than ordinary language variation.
notes: High — systematic safety benchmark for VLAs; relevant to verification and safety evaluation of visuomotor policies

title: Constrained Flow Matching via Lagrangian Dual Flows
authors: Vince Kurtz, Alexander Davydov
headline: Lagrangian dual dynamics guarantee nonlinear constraint satisfaction in flow matching without projection
summary: Lagrangian Dual Flows enable constrained generation by flowing a dual co-state alongside samples, guaranteeing nonlinear constraint satisfaction without expensive optimization, pseudoinverses, or projection during denoising. The method opens theoretical connections between flow matching and primal-dual optimization, with applications to robotics and planning.
abstract: Flow matching is a powerful tool for generative modeling, but emerging applications in robotics, planning, and physics require inference-time constraints on generated outputs. Such constraints are often complex and highly nonlinear. As a result, methods designed for linear constraints like image inpainting are rarely sufficient, and projection or optimization-based alternatives can be prohibitively expensive. In this paper, we introduce Lagrangian Dual Flows, a new family of constrained generation techniques based on Lagrangian dual dynamics. By simply flowing a dual co-state alongside generated samples, we can guarantee nonlinear constraint satisfaction without expensive optimization subproblems, pseudoinverses, or projection steps during the denoising process. The resulting constrained generation algorithms are simple, effective, and open new theoretical connections between flow matching and primal-dual methods in numerical optimization.
notes: High — constrained flow matching with guaranteed constraint satisfaction; relevant to safe generative policy control

title: Optimal Transport Q-Learning for Flow Policy Steering and Acceleration
authors: Andreas Sochopoulos, Esmeralda S. Whitammer, Nikolaos Tsagkas, Joao Moura, Michael Gienger, Sethu Vijayakumar
headline: RL post-training boosts flow policy success from 36% to 86% while cutting inference steps by 70%
summary: OTQL introduces advantage-weighted conditional optimal transport flow matching for fine-tuning suboptimal flow-based policies using RL post-training. With only 50-60 interaction episodes, OTQL increases single-task policy success from 36% to 86% and VLA success from 38% to 76%, while reducing inference steps by 70%.
abstract: Diffusion and flow policies have recently demonstrated remarkable performance in robotic applications by accurately capturing multimodal robot trajectory distributions, especially in the context of vision language action (VLA) models. However, high quality policy performance also requires fast inference and high quality demonstrations, which are often hard to get, and lack of these leads to suboptimal policy behaviors and failure under distribution shifts. This paper addresses the problem of fine-tuning and accelerating suboptimal flow-based policies using the robot's experience through RL post-training. We introduce Optimal Transport Q-Learning (OTQL), a new methodology for finetuning flow policies using advantage weighted conditional optimal transport flow matching. OTQL can finetune and accelerate flows with an interaction budget of 50-60 episodes while avoiding computationally expensive distillation in simulation and real-world robot tasks, increasing average success percentage of single-task policies from 36% to 86% and of a pre-trained VLA from 38% to 76% while reducing the number of inference steps per action generation by 70%.
notes: High — RL post-training for flow policies with significant acceleration; relevant to flow matching + RL intersection

title: PriGo: Test-Time Primitive Guidance to Diffusion and Flow Policies for Adaptive Robotic Manipulation
authors: Zezeng Li, Enda Xiang, Thuy Tran, Di Huang, Momath Thiam, Liming Chen
headline: Primitive-guided test-time adaptation improves pretrained diffusion/flow policies without retraining
summary: PriGo introduces primitive-guided test-time adaptation for robotic manipulation, using a primitive classifier (PANet) that predicts primitive distributions from observations and a differentiable guidance mechanism that constrains action generation during inference. PriGo seamlessly integrates into pretrained diffusion and flow policies without retraining, working with both lightweight policies and large VLA models.
abstract: PriGo introduces primitive-guided test-time adaptation for robotic manipulation policies. The framework consists of two components: a primitive classifier PANet that predicts primitive distributions from observations, and a differentiable primitive guidance mechanism that constrains action generation during inference. PriGo can be seamlessly integrated into pretrained diffusion and flow policies without retraining. It works with both lightweight policies and large VLA models, effectively decoupling discrete primitive planning from continuous action learning.
notes: High — test-time guidance for diffusion/flow policies; relevant to inference-time policy steering

title: ReconVLA: An Uncertainty-Guided and Failure-Aware Vision-Language-Action Framework for Robotic Control
authors: Lingling Chen, Zongyao Lyu, William J. Beksi
matched_interests: Conformal prediction|Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs)|Verification of visuomotor policies
headline: Conformal prediction on VLA action tokens yields calibrated uncertainty for failure detection without retraining
summary: ReconVLA applies conformal prediction directly to action token outputs of pretrained VLA policies, yielding calibrated uncertainty estimates that correlate with execution quality. It extends conformal prediction to robot state space for outlier/unsafe state detection. Results show conformalized predictions improve failure anticipation and reduce catastrophic errors without retraining the underlying VLA.
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as generalist robotic controllers capable of mapping visual observations and natural language instructions to continuous action sequences. However, VLAs provide no calibrated measure of confidence in their action predictions, thus limiting their reliability in real-world settings where uncertainty and failures must be anticipated. To address this problem we introduce ReconVLA, a reliable conformal model that produces uncertainty-guided and failure-aware control signals. Concretely, our approach applies conformal prediction directly to the action token outputs of pretrained VLA policies, yielding calibrated uncertainty estimates that correlate with execution quality and task success. Furthermore, we extend conformal prediction to the robot state space to detect outliers or unsafe states before failures occur, providing a simple yet effective failure detection mechanism that complements the action-level uncertainty. We evaluate ReconVLA in both simulation and real robot experiments across diverse manipulation tasks. Our results show that conformalized action predictions consistently improve failure anticipation, reduce catastrophic errors, and provide a calibrated measure of confidence without retraining or modifying the underlying VLA.
notes: Core — conformal prediction applied to VLAs for calibrated uncertainty and failure detection; directly relevant to verification of visuomotor policies

title: Augmented Lagrangian Multiplier Network for State-wise Safety in Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jiaming Zhang, Yujie Yang, Yao Lyu, Shengbo Eben Li, Liping Zhang
headline: Augmented Lagrangian multiplier networks stabilize state-wise safe RL and outperform baselines
summary: ALaM introduces an augmented Lagrangian framework for stable learning of state-wise safety multipliers in RL. A quadratic penalty compensates for delayed updates while the multiplier network trains via supervised regression. Theoretically guarantees multiplier convergence; the SAC-ALaM algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art safe RL baselines in both safety and return.
abstract: Safety is a primary challenge in real-world reinforcement learning (RL). Formulating safety requirements as state-wise constraints has become a prominent paradigm. Handling state-wise constraints with the Lagrangian method requires a distinct multiplier for every state, necessitating neural networks to approximate them as a multiplier network. However, applying standard dual gradient ascent to multiplier networks induces severe training oscillations. This is because the inherent instability of dual ascent is exacerbated by network generalization -- local overshoots and delayed updates propagate to adjacent states, further amplifying policy fluctuations. Existing stabilization techniques are designed for scalar multipliers, which are inadequate for state-dependent multiplier networks. To address this challenge, we propose an augmented Lagrangian multiplier network (ALaM) framework for stable learning of state-wise multipliers. ALaM consists of two key components. First, a quadratic penalty is introduced into the augmented Lagrangian to compensate for delayed multiplier updates and establish the local convexity near the optimum, thereby mitigating policy oscillations. Second, the multiplier network is trained via supervised regression toward a dual target, which stabilizes training and promotes convergence. Theoretically, we show that ALaM guarantees multiplier convergence and thus recovers the optimal policy of the constrained problem.
notes: High — state-wise safe RL with multiplier network stability guarantees; relevant to safe robot control

title: D-SafeMPC: Diffusion-Driven Safe Model Predictive Control with Discrete-Time Control Barrier Functions
authors: Erdi Sayar, Ersin Daş, Joel W. Burdick, Alois Knoll, Erdal Kayacan
matched_interests: Diffusion models|Safe & robust robot control|Control Barrier Functions (CBFs)
headline: Diffusion-based MPC generates trajectories filtered by discrete-time control barrier functions for provable safety
summary: D-SafeMPC integrates a diffusion model for trajectory generation with discrete-time control barrier functions (DCBFs) to enforce hard safety constraints inside a model predictive control loop. The diffusion sampler proposes candidate action sequences that are then projected onto the safe set defined by the DCBFs, coupling generative planning flexibility with formal constraint satisfaction. The approach targets safety-critical robotic systems where learned generative planners must not violate state/actuation limits. Accepted for oral presentation at CLAWAR 2026.
abstract: A key challenge in robotics is generating safe and feasible trajectories for complex dynamical systems. Diffusion models have shown strong capability in generating diverse, high-quality trajectories, but they often lack formal safety guarantees. This paper presents D-SafeMPC, a diffusion-driven safe model predictive control framework that integrates a diffusion-based trajectory generator with discrete-time control barrier functions (DCBFs). The diffusion model proposes candidate trajectories, which are refined through an MPC optimization augmented with DCBF constraints to guarantee forward invariance of the safe set at every step. This combination leverages the expressiveness of generative diffusion planning while enforcing formal safety through barrier certificates. Experiments on robotic control tasks demonstrate that the method produces safe, feasible trajectories and outperforms baselines in constraint satisfaction and trajectory quality. (Abstract summarized from arXiv/search metadata; see paper for verbatim text.)
notes: Alert: Tomlin/Bansal/Herbert. High — diffusion trajectory generation coupled with discrete-time CBFs for safe MPC; intersects diffusion methods and safety-critical control

title: Mem-World: Memory-Augmented Action-Conditioned World Models for Persistent Robot Manipulation
authors: Zirui Zheng, Jiaqian Yu, Xiongfeng Peng, Jun Shi, Mingyi Li, Chao Zhang, Weiming Li, Dong Wang, Huchuan Lu, Xu Jia
headline: Surfel-indexed 4D memory lets action-conditioned world models stay consistent through occlusions in long manipulation rollouts
summary: Mem-World is a memory-augmented, multi-view, action-conditioned world model for persistent robot manipulation. Its core component, W-VMem, is a 4D wrist-view-centered surfel-indexed memory that anchors historical observations to temporally evolving surface elements, enabling geometry-aware retrieval of relevant past frames under end-effector occlusion and rapid wrist-camera motion. The method produces more temporally consistent long-horizon rollouts, improves the Pearson correlation of imagined policy evaluation with real-world performance by 14.5% over Ctrl-World, and boosts long-horizon success rates from 58% to 72% when used as a synthetic data engine.
abstract: Action-conditioned world models have emerged as a promising paradigm for robot learning, offering a scalable alternative to costly real-world experimentation by generating action-consistent video rollouts. However, persistent world modeling remains challenging in manipulation: frequent end-effector occlusions and rapid wrist-camera motion make the current observation insufficient for predicting future views, causing models to forget or hallucinate scene details seen in earlier frames. Existing memory retrieval strategies often fail to identify informative history in dynamic manipulation scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose Mem-World, a memory-augmented multi-view action-conditioned world model. At its core, we present W-VMem, a 4D wrist-view-centered surfel-indexed memory that anchors historical observations to temporally evolving surface elements. By explicitly modeling when and where scene elements are observed, W-VMem enables geometry-aware retrieval of relevant history frames conditioned on future actions. During generation, relevant history frames are selected via surfel-based rendering and scoring, providing informative and non-redundant context for prediction. Extensive experiments show that Mem-World generates persistent rollouts in complex manipulation scenarios, enables more reliable policy evaluation than Ctrl-World, improving the Pearson correlation with real-world performance by 14.5%, and supports effective policy improvement through synthetic data generation, increasing success rates from 58% to 72% on long-horizon tasks.
notes: Alert: Majumdar. Core — action-conditioned world model whose main use case is reliable policy evaluation and improvement; directly relevant to world-model-based verification of learned policies

title: WorldBagel: Uncovering the Power of Unified Multimodal Models for Vision-Language-Action-World Modeling
authors: Zelin Zhao, Min Shi, Bo Yuan, Haotian Xue, Jialuo Li, Lama Moukheiber, Humphrey Shi, Yongxin Chen
matched_interests: World models for robotics|Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs)|Generalist policies
headline: Unified multimodal model as a Vision-Language-Action-World model beats task-specific alternatives on manipulation
summary: WorldBagel is a unified vision-language-action-world (VLAW) framework built on the BAGEL multimodal model, used to systematically study whether unification helps world modeling for robotics. Across multi-task robotic manipulation and cross-domain experiments (LIBERO, Language Table, Franka), unified models consistently outperform task-specific alternatives and learn higher-quality, more structured action representations that are semantically aligned with visual and linguistic context. The results argue that unification itself benefits effective VLAW modeling and yields deeper insight into multimodal world models.
abstract: World models aim to capture environment dynamics to support perception, reasoning, and action, and have recently risen as a prominent direction in Vision-Language-Action-World (VLAW) modeling. While recent unified vision-language models demonstrate unprecedented multimodal generation ability, their role as world models remains largely uncovered. We introduce WorldBagel, a unified VLAW framework built on BAGEL, a modern multimodal unified model, and use it to systematically study the impact of unification in VLAW modeling. Through multi-task robotic manipulation and cross-domain experiments, unified models consistently outperform task-specific alternatives and learn higher-quality action representations that are more structured and semantically aligned with visual and linguistic context. Results on LIBERO, Language Table, and Franka suggest that unification itself benefits learning effective VLAW models, yielding both consistent empirical gains and deeper insights into multimodal world modeling. (Abstract from arXiv/search metadata.)
notes: Alert: Bajcsy. Core — unifies world modeling with vision-language-action policy learning; sits at the world-models / generalist-policy intersection

title: SSI-Policy: Learning Structured Scene Interfaces for Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation
authors: Kaijun Wang, Zikai Ouyang, Xuping Wu, Jinyi Hong, Wei Pan, Haibo Lu, Jia Pan, Wei Zhang, Linfang Zheng
headline: RGB-only structured scene interface enables few-shot vision-language manipulation from just 10 demonstrations
summary: SSI-Policy is a modular manipulation framework built around a Structured Scene Interface (SSI): a unified, RGB-only intermediate representation that jointly encodes monocular depth features, language-grounded object layouts, and instruction-conditioned 2D motion trajectories. Because SSI is robot-agnostic and trainable from action-free video, it decouples perception from control so the downstream policy can learn from as few as 10 demonstrations per task. On LIBERO it improves over the strongest prior method by nearly 15% with only 10 demos and stays competitive with 50-demo methods using large-scale pretraining, and it validates on 13 real-world tasks spanning spatial reasoning, cross-embodiment transfer, and contact-rich manipulation. Accepted to IROS 2026.
abstract: Real-world robotic manipulation demands spatial grounding, task-aware reasoning, and precise control. Learning such capabilities becomes particularly challenging in the low-data regime. Prior methods often trade off scalable task-level reasoning and explicit physical structure: video-based approaches can drift geometrically over long horizons, 3D approaches often require depth sensing, and many flow/trajectory interfaces emphasize motion without an explicit RGB-only geometric representation. We introduce SSI-Policy, a modular framework built around a Structured Scene Interface (SSI) -- a unified, RGB-only intermediate representation that jointly encodes monocular depth features, language-grounded object layouts, and instruction-conditioned 2D motion trajectories. Critically, SSI is robot-agnostic and trainable from action-free video, decoupling perception from control so that the downstream policy can learn from few demonstrations. On the LIBERO benchmark with only 10 demonstrations per task, SSI-Policy improves over the strongest prior method by nearly 15% and remains competitive with 50-demo methods that leverage large-scale external pretraining. Ablations show that geometric and motion cues provide complementary benefits within the shared interface. We further validate on 13 real-world tasks spanning spatial reasoning, cross-embodiment transfer, and contact-rich manipulation.
notes: Alert: Bajcsy. High — structured intermediate representation for few-shot, cross-embodiment vision-language manipulation policies

title: Present but Not Remembered: Auditing How Frozen VLAs Encode, Deploy, and Steer Visual History
authors: Chih-Ting Liao, Xin Cao
matched_interests: Verification of visuomotor policies|Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs)|Adversarial robustness of robot policies
headline: Training-free audit shows frozen VLAs store history redundantly and only use it when the current frame is lost
summary: This paper presents a reusable, training-free temporal-deployment audit of how frozen vision-language-action models handle recent past observations at each step. The authors find that past-frame content is linearly decodable at every network depth, but the information unique to history beyond the current frame is essentially zero—stored history is a redundant copy of the present. History is only causally deployed into the action under near-total loss of the current frame, and while the encoding is identical across architectures, the deployment regime flips between models. The work is directly relevant to verifying and characterizing the behavior of black-box visuomotor policies.
abstract: A frozen vision-language-action model (VLA) receives a short window of recent observations at every step. We ask what the model already does with the history it receives, auditing how frozen VLAs encode, deploy, and steer visual history. We find that (i) past-frame content is linearly decodable at every depth, but the information unique to history beyond the current frame is essentially zero—the stored history is a redundant copy of the present; (ii) history is causally deployed into the action only under near-total loss of the current frame; and (iii) across architectures the encoding is identical, but the deployment regime flips between different models. We present our measurements as a reusable, training-free temporal-deployment audit for probing visuomotor policies. (Abstract from arXiv/search metadata.)
notes: Alert: Tomlin (citation). Core — training-free auditing/verification of the internal temporal behavior of black-box visuomotor policies; closely aligned with verification of visuomotor policies

title: Look Before You Leap: Distilling Tree Search into Action Evaluation for Frozen VLA Models
authors: Xinyi Xie, Zican Hu, Zhanyu Liu, Yicheng Dong, Wei Wu, Zhi Sun, et al.
headline: Distilling MCTS into a Q-value evaluator lets frozen VLAs pick better actions without a simulator
summary: The paper argues that VLA failures stem not only from action generation but from action evaluation: frozen VLAs already contain competent behaviors in their output distribution, with success rising from 33% at pass@1 to 92% at pass@32. It proposes SVA (Search, Value, and Act), which uses Monte-Carlo tree search in simulation to explore the VLA's output distribution and collect return-annotated trajectories, then distills this into a lightweight Q-value model predicting the expected consequence of candidate actions. At deployment the frozen VLA proposes several candidates and the evaluator selects the one with the highest uncertainty-regularized Q-value, requiring no simulator access.
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) failures stem not only from action generation but also from action evaluation. A diagnostic study confirms that frozen VLAs already contain competent behaviors in their output distribution, with overall success rates rising from 33% at pass@1 to 92% at pass@32. We propose SVA (Search, Value, and Act), a framework that equips frozen VLA policies with long-term consequence awareness. SVA first uses Monte-Carlo tree search in simulation to fully explore the VLA's output distribution and collect diverse trajectories annotated with empirical returns; this knowledge is then distilled into a lightweight Q-value model that predicts the expected consequence of candidate actions. At deployment, the frozen VLA proposes multiple candidates and the evaluator selects the one with the highest uncertainty-regularized Q-value, requiring no simulator access. (Abstract from arXiv/search metadata.)
notes: Alert: Bajcsy/Majumdar. High — value-based action evaluation for frozen VLA policies; combines MCTS-distilled Q-learning with generalist policy deployment

title: GemNav: Discrete-Token Visual Robot Navigation using a Multimodal Large Language Model
authors: Peter Bohm, Saimunur Rahman, Abdelwahed Khamis, Sagun Man Singh Shrestha, Chris McCool, Peyman Moghadam
headline: LoRA-adapted frozen MLLM navigates via discrete waypoint tokens, transferring zero-shot from 8.7 hours of data
summary: GemNav adapts a frozen multimodal large language model for short-to-medium-horizon waypoint navigation using LoRA on the language tower alone, with no auxiliary visual encoder and no continuous regression head. Waypoints and categorical navigation signals share a single discrete token vocabulary emitted by the language-model head, and a soft-decoded auxiliary loss recovers the metric structure that pure cross-entropy training discards. Trained on a single 8.7-hour open corpus—roughly three orders of magnitude smaller than competing sets—it transfers zero-shot to four unseen environments, stopping within 0.25–0.42 m of the goal across 20 real-world trials. The results show discrete-token adaptation of frozen MLLMs as a data-efficient, deployable route to foundation-model robot navigation.
abstract: GemNav is a visual robot navigation policy that adapts a frozen Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) for short-to-medium horizon waypoint navigation using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on the language tower alone, with no auxiliary visual encoder and no continuous regression head. Waypoints and categorical navigation signals share a single discrete token vocabulary generated by the language-model head, and a soft-decoded auxiliary loss recovers the metric structure that pure cross-entropy training discards. On a single 8.7-hour open corpus, roughly three orders of magnitude smaller than competing training sets, the policy transfers zero-shot to four physically distinct unseen environments and stops within 0.25-0.42 m of the goal across 20 real-world trials covering an open carpark, an obstacle carpark, a long outdoor chemical yard, and an indoor warehouse. These results indicate that discrete-token adaptation of frozen MLLMs can provide a data-efficient, deployable alternative for foundation model robot navigation. (Abstract from arXiv/search metadata.)
notes: Alert: Majumdar. Moderate — data-efficient adaptation of a frozen MLLM into a deployable navigation policy; foundation-model / generalist policy angle

title: Reachability-Preserving Bellman Operator for the Discounted Reach-Cost Value Function: Uniting Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability and Reinforcement Learning
authors: Isabelle El-Hajj, Prashant Solanki, Jasper van Beers, Coen de Visser, Erik-Jan van Kampen
matched_interests: Hamilton-Jacobi reachability|Reinforcement learning|Safe & robust robot control
headline: A contractive reach-cost Bellman operator whose fixed point exactly matches the HJ reachability value function
summary: This paper closes the gap between Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability—which gives rigorous safety guarantees but suffers the curse of dimensionality—and deep RL, which is scalable but sample-based. Building on a semantics-preserving discounted reach-based value function, the authors derive a non-additive Bellman operator whose unique fixed point exactly matches the HJ value function, and prove that discounting makes the operator contractive, yielding existence, uniqueness, and convergence of value iteration. The result is a principled, semantically exact bridge that lets learning-based methods approximate reachability value functions while preserving their safety-critical meaning.
abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides rigorous safety and reachability guarantees for continuous-time dynamical systems, but its numerical solution suffers from the curse of dimensionality, while deep reinforcement learning (DRL) offers scalable sample-based methods. We close this gap by building on a semantics-preserving discounted reach-based value function and deriving a non-additive Bellman operator whose unique fixed point exactly matches the value function in the HJ formulation. We prove that discounting makes this operator contractive, yielding existence, uniqueness, and convergence of value iteration. This yields a principled and semantically exact connection between HJ reachability and RL, enabling learning-based methods to approximate reachability value functions while preserving their safety-critical meaning. (Abstract from arXiv/search metadata.)
notes: Alert: Fan/Herbert/Bajcsy. High — formal, semantics-exact bridge between HJ reachability and RL; relevant to scalable, learning-based safety verification

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning using Ideas from Model Predictive Control
authors: Georg Schäfer, Jakob Rehrl, Stefan Huber, Simon Hirlaender
headline: Borrowing model-predictive-control ideas to keep reinforcement learning safe during training and deployment
summary: This paper develops a safe reinforcement learning approach that imports ideas from model predictive control to constrain policy behavior and improve safety during learning and execution. By combining the receding-horizon, constraint-aware structure of MPC with RL's data-driven policy optimization, the method aims to reduce constraint violations while retaining RL's adaptivity. It is positioned as a practical bridge between classical constrained control and modern learning-based control. Accepted at Eurocast 2026.
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables agents to learn control policies through interaction, but ensuring safety during and after learning remains a central challenge. This work develops a safe reinforcement learning approach that leverages ideas from model predictive control (MPC): the receding-horizon, constraint-aware structure of MPC is used to shape and constrain the RL policy so that safety requirements are respected during training and deployment. By integrating MPC-style constraint handling with RL policy optimization, the method reduces constraint violations while preserving the adaptivity and performance benefits of learning-based control. Experiments demonstrate improved safety compared to standard RL baselines. (Abstract from arXiv/search metadata.)
notes: Alert: Tomlin/Bansal/Herbert. Moderate — MPC-inspired constraint handling for safe RL; standard safe-learning-control intersection

title: Learning-enabled Parameter Synthesis for Nonlinear Systems from Signal Temporal Logic
authors: Alex Beaudin, Hanna Krasowski, Eric Palanques-Tost, Calin Belta, Murat Arcak
matched_interests: Safe & robust robot control|Signal Temporal Logic (STL)
headline: Gradient optimization plus set-based reachability synthesizes parameters that provably satisfy continuous-time STL
summary: This work synthesizes parameters for nonlinear systems that robustly satisfy continuous-time Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications under uncertain initial conditions. It combines gradient-based optimization with set-based reachability verification to search high-dimensional parameter spaces efficiently while providing provable satisfaction guarantees for the optimized parameters. The method is demonstrated on three systems with up to 18 parameter dimensions, showing scalable, guarantee-carrying synthesis.
abstract: We propose to synthesize parameters for nonlinear systems that robustly satisfy continuous-time Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications for uncertain initial conditions. Our method uses gradient-based optimization together with set-based reachability verification to efficiently learn in high-dimensional parameter spaces while providing provable satisfaction guarantees for the optimized parameters. We demonstrate the approach on three systems with up to 18 parameter dimensions, showing that it scales to high-dimensional synthesis problems while retaining formal guarantees. (Abstract from arXiv/search metadata.)
notes: Alert: Lindemann. Moderate — couples gradient-based (learning-enabled) synthesis with reachability verification and STL guarantees; verification-adjacent formal methods

title: Cost-Aware Active Perception for k-step Predictive Safety
authors: Sumukha Udupa, Jie Fu
headline: Scheduling sensor queries under a budget to maximize information about future-state safety
summary: This paper synthesizes active perception policies for predictive safety monitoring in partially observable stochastic systems, where a monitor dynamically schedules sensor queries under strict sensing/communication budgets to maximize information about the safety of future states. The dynamics are modeled as a labeled hidden Markov model with safety requirements given by a deterministic finite automaton, and the objective minimizes k-step Shannon conditional entropy of future-state safety under a limited query budget. Using observable operators, the authors derive an efficient algorithm to compute k-step conditional entropy and analyze the gradient of that entropy with respect to policy parameters, enabling cost-aware active sensing for safety.
abstract: This work studies the synthesis of active perception policies for predictive safety monitoring in partially observable stochastic systems, where the monitor dynamically schedules sensor queries under strict sensing and communication budgets to maximize information gain about the safety of future states. The underlying stochastic dynamics are captured by a labeled hidden Markov model (HMM) with safety requirements defined by a deterministic finite automaton (DFA), and the method minimizes k-step Shannon conditional entropy of the safety of future states as a planning objective under a limited sensor query budget. Using observable operators, we derive an efficient algorithm to compute the k-step conditional entropy and analyze key properties of the conditional entropy gradient with respect to policy parameters. (Abstract from arXiv/search metadata; arXiv preprint titled 'Information-Driven Active Perception for k-step Predictive Safety Monitoring'.)
notes: Alert: Bajcsy/Herbert. High — active/information-driven perception scheduling for predictive safety monitoring; ties active learning to safety verification

title: An Update to the Level Set Theorems in Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability Analysis
authors: Dylan Hirsch, William McEneaney, Jaime Fisac, Claire Tomlin, Sylvia Herbert
headline: Technical update to Hamilton-Jacobi reachability's Level Set Theorems, adding criteria for validity
summary: Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability (HJR) relies on Level Set Theorems that connect the value function of an HJ PDE to qualitative goals like goal-reaching or obstacle-avoidance.
